doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

chapter: Family and life on the road
title: Pete's Place sitcom in Toronto
summary: A series set in a Vegas club with guest comics he fitted into frameworks.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I think a lot of them did. Because I’ve never been able to write. Oddly enough now I could write for TV, for sketches because I did a series in Toronto called Pete’s Place. It took place in Vegas but we shot it in Toronto. And the deal was I had a small club off the strip in Vegas and everything went wrong that could go wrong with the club you know. The mob tried to move in and this and that. And so I asked a bunch of my friends to come up and I put people together that had never been together before to see if the sparks would fly, and it really worked beautifully. Like Phyllis Diller and Irwin Corey. Dick Shawn and Pat McCormick, the guy who wrote the Tonight Show. I put all these crazy people together and it worked great. They had fun and you know, they got along great. But yeah, I enjoyed that series. It was fun to do. And the opening was cute too. It showed a Rolls Royce going down the strip in Vegas at night, the marquees — Frank Sinatra, Wayne Newton, Elvis Presley — and then the camera — the Rolls Royce stops at a red light and the camera pans back and it shows the driver up front with his proper dress. And I’m sitting in the back of the Rolls Royce with a big cigar you know in my tuxedo. And then the light turns green and the Rolls pulls away and I’m on a bicycle next to it. And I have my trumpet hanging on the handle bars. So I walked up to this club and it’s the same Roman printing that’s on Caesar’s Palace. It said, “Pete’s Place.” And I look up and the L falls out and then it just — or it says, “Pete’s Palace” and the L falls out it just says Pete’s Place.

Yeah. I could write those routines for these people because I’d write frameworks, because all these people were great. You know and I’d say I’m not going to tell you what to say, you know I’m going to do this. You know Morey Amsterdam and you know like they know a million jokes. So I’m not going to tell you — here’s the framework. We do this and from here you go outside, just remember the ending is when I drop the glass on the floor and you say this and then we go to commercial. And it worked great. We did 50 shows, and they were good.
